messages:
Marta - Procurement: Quick vendor question — QuotaFlex sent a renewal proposal and the commercial team framed two different licensing structures. I attached the pdf in Drive: https://drive.google.com/qf-proposal. We need a quick thumbs on cost + operational pain (seat management vs pure usage). cc @Sanjay (ML Eng) @Alex (Finance) 

Sanjay (ML Eng): Can you paste the numbers from the quote? seat + pool vs per-embedding price would help. Our embeddings workload is heavy (search and personalization).

Alex (Finance): Also include invoicing cadence, payment terms, and overage definition. Seats increase fixed spend and headcount mapping could be annoying. Usage = variable but easier to audit.

Ting Li (Platform): Do they allow pooling across projects / orgs? If reserved embeddings are pooled it could be simpler. Also: any per-model routing SLA attached to seat tiers?

Marta - Procurement: Pasting the relevant excerpt from the quote below:

```
Option A - Seat + Reserved Units:
  10 seats @ $850/mo = $8,500/mo
  Included: 500M embeddings/month pooled across seats
  Overage: $0.000010 per embedding
  Support: Standard (SLA upgrade at additional cost)
Option B - Pure Usage:
  $0.000020 per embedding
  Volume tiers: >1B/quarter = 15% discount
  30-day invoicing, NET30
Notes: 12-month term quoted, data residency in us-west available
```

Sanjay (ML Eng): Rough back-of-envelope: we’re at ~120M embeddings/month right now (~1.44B/yr). At Option B (no discount) annual = 1.44B * 0.00002 = $28,800. Option A annual seats = $8,500*12 = $102,000 (includes 500M/month so no overage today). So for raw $/embed usage looks cheaper on pure usage. But Option A buys predictability + possible enterprise features.

Alex (Finance): Exactly — usage looks materially cheaper today. But the seat option transfers risk to us (high fixed spend). We should ask for a hybrid: smaller reserved pool + usage overlay. Also ask vendor to cap annual increases and provide credits for sustained outages.

Ting Li (Platform): If we can pool 500M across org and burst with usage overlay, that might be best. Ask whether included units apply to embeddings only or also generation calls. Also confirm how they meter: per-embedding call, vector size, or per-token? Need exact metering logic.

QuotaFlex Rep: Hi Marta — thanks for the ping. We can do a hybrid: 5 seats + 300M included + usage overlay at $0.000012/embedding. Alternatively, pure usage with a 12-month commit gives 15% off the listed rate. We can also provide a sample invoice and SOW for legal review. Happy to put a cap on price increases and add a 99.9% availability SLA on the enterprise package.

Marta - Procurement: Perfect — please send the revised quote and sample invoice. Also include the meter definition and a short clause about overage calculation. Can you confirm whether included units are pooled org-wide?

QuotaFlex Rep: Will do. Included units are pooled at the org level for seats. I’ll send a revised quote today and attach the sample invoice.

Marta - Procurement: @Procurement-Bot create a PR and approval workflow once the revised quote lands. I want legal and finance looped before signing.

Procurement-Bot: Created PR #462: "QuotaFlex - eval & review". Approvers requested: Alex (Finance), Legal, Security. Link: https://procurement.internal/pr/462

Alex (Finance): Please also ask for a short trial invoice that shows how usage/overage would be billed in a peak month — we need to model forecast impact on committed spend.

Marta - Procurement: Noted. I’ll ask for a sample peak-month invoice and confirm data residency and termination terms (60-day wind-down, data export).

Sanjay (ML Eng): One more ask from eng: can they provide p95 latency numbers for embedding endpoints under 0.5ms target for our smaller requests? If not, we might push for lower included unit price instead.

QuotaFlex Rep: Will include latency SLAs and sample metrics. Expect the revised package and documents by EOD.

Marta - Procurement: Thanks everyone. I’ll post the revised quote here when received and we can triage before PR approval. :thumbsup:
